title: Does Minoxidil Work For Hair Loss? What The Evidence Says
meta: Minoxidil beats placebo for male pattern hair loss, but it takes 3 to 6 months, you have to keep using it, and the shedding at the start is normal.
answer_first: Yes, for male pattern hair loss, and the effect is real but moderate. Topical minoxidil raises hair count compared with placebo, and you need 3 to 6 months before the result is worth judging. It only holds while you keep using it, so treat it as ongoing maintenance rather than a fix.
h2: How long before you can judge it
The shedding phase people quit during

faq.a: Give it 3 to 6 months before you decide. Most trials read results at that point, and almost all of them run 12 months or less, so nobody can tell you much about year five.

faq.q: Why is my hair shedding more since I started?
faq.a: Shedding in the first weeks is common and it is not a sign the drug is failing. It is the usual reason people quit early.
The hair you gained is lost within months of stopping. This is maintenance, not a one-off course.

faq.q: My scalp is itchy and flaking, is that the minoxidil?
faq.a: Possibly. Contact dermatitis is the most frequent adverse effect, and propylene glycol in the liquid vehicle is usually behind it. A foam without it tends to be better tolerated. Ask a clinician rather than pushing through it.

claims.text: Topical minoxidil is approved at 2 percent and 5 percent for androgenetic alopecia.
Shedding in the first weeks of minoxidil is common and does not mean the drug is failing.
Hair gained on minoxidil is lost within months of stopping, so it has to be used continuously.
Topical minoxidil increases hair count versus placebo in men with androgenetic alopecia, with moderate effect sizes.
Minoxidil results take 3 to 6 months to read, and most trials run 12 months or less.
Irritant and allergic contact dermatitis is the most frequent adverse effect of topical minoxidil.
Propylene glycol in the solution vehicle is the usual culprit for dermatitis, and foam formulations without it are better tolerated.
